summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with atypical chest pain radiating to the neck, arm, and back, following a recent hospitalization for similar symptoms. He had stopped cardiac medications previously, raising concern for stent thrombosis, but serial troponins were negative and a stress test showed no new blockages. Initial fevers and leukocytosis resolved without evidence of infection. He developed opiate withdrawal symptoms during admission, which were managed with clonidine and diazepam. His symptoms improved, and he expressed motivation to remain abstinent from opioids. He was discharged home with continued cardiac medications, referrals for addiction support, and follow-up plans.
problems: Coronary atherosclerosis of native coronary artery
